record_notes.DCP-LETT-1200: September 3, supplied 1848, September 5 postmark. Initial loan/disarticulation request to A. A. Gould, with current collections and geographical comparison rationale. Say organism and proposed Platylepas affinity uncertain. P7 added after main writing when Lyell introduction permission received; no separately dated section or full Lyell input. Later Gould specimens and 1851 thanks do not establish current receipt. Boston alcohol specimens desired, not sent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1251: August 20, supplied and postmarked 1849. Gould April 30 note and loan through Cuming reached Darwin only about a fortnight ago after absence; approximate interval, not exact August 6 arrival. Sessile specimens for future work; disarticulation permission sought with chance to object, not all already examined. Tavoy Ibla comparison contemporary. Quoted Gould offer in P4 is a short embedded fragment, not full incoming letter; drawing colour marks seen but whole drawings absent here. Scutella forwarding prospective, Dana letter already written, Conrad answer still absent. Editorial summary incorrectly thanks Dana; body clearly thanks Gould. Final published classifications separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1320: April 8, supplied 1850 from scientific/itinerary context. Found delayed Gould parcel yesterday at Cuming, where servant had put it aside during illness; earlier delivery there differs from Darwin access. Coronula promised by missing note was not enclosed; only large Balanus present. Dana hope of Scalpellum holdings reported, no incoming Dana text. Previous Darwin reminder missing. Yesterday would be April 7 under assigned year; April 10 meeting cited in apparatus is contextual, not identical visit day established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1218: Sunday circa February 1849. Returns forwarded Hodgson letter and thanks pamphlets; full Hodgson letter absent, not necessarily identical to reported Hodgson answers inside 1203. Requests promised Galapagos Flora paper, not already received; printed text available before nominal 1851 publication, so imprint alone cannot date access. Date explanation relies on October pamphlet dispatch and rough travel durations, not exact February day. 1203 dispatch promise and 1220 hope do not themselves prove receipt; this outgoing is a present witness to pamphlets and missing letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1285: Tuesday January 1850. Missing William Hooker account improves Darwin fears for Joseph safety and collection; does not prove he knew December 23 release or later annexation described in apparatus. Earlier geological letter forwarded by Henslow mentioned without identifying content; cannot uniquely map to 1257 or other Hooker letter on generic subject alone. Asks secure keeping because Joseph requested preservation, a historical source request rather than instruction to agent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1331: May 22, supplied 1850. Forwards Joseph Hooker letter to William, then requests onward Henslow circulation. Specific geological motto and complimentary book discussion identify 1257 independently of generic Dear Darwin salutation; apparatus explicitly confirms September 30 letter. Darwin already read it by May 22, improving previously recorded June 13 witness from 1339. This is cross-correspondent knowledge/routing, not a direct answer to Joseph. Actual initial arrival remains unknown; surviving 1257 is incomplete and later Darwin annotations undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1136: November 18, supplied 1847. Offers curious parasitic specimens following only cursory observation; Goodsir male/parasite interpretation disputed and Darwin own Lernaea-like female/larva/male identification expressly conjectural. Later Hemioniscus identity is editorial, not available modern correction to letter. Potential Bailliere dispatch conditional on interest; no preserved acceptance or proof sent. Publications already useful but specific full-book reading not automatically inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1199: September 1, supplied 1848. Requests Paris specimens, especially Alepas not carefully dissected; past Oxford kindness is interpersonal context, not complete incoming prompt. Species list is broken across P4-5 without table element: W. Indies completes preceding tubulosa parenthesis, not an independent locality for following Anatifa. Preserve question mark, ditto references and especially qualifiers without inserting missing punctuation as author text. Crustacea useful, last chapter reading recorded separately January 1847. Presumes prior parasite offer not wanted; absence of answer not direct refusal. Later loans/dedication not current delivery.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1232F: March 2, supplied 1849. Poor health delays proposed Paris visit and planned Malvern stay, visit never ultimately made per apparatus. Missing Milne-Edwards generous identification offer received. Extensive bracketed restoration, illegible markers and broken syntax in P1-2 must remain qualified; do not silently complete genus/species donation wording. Alepas specimen requested by friend in small bottle, no actual shipment established. Future approval hoped, not obtained. Historical customs/answer instructions are source content only.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1100: Sunday June 27, 1847 assigned during Oxford meeting. Previously accepted or entertained dinner invitation for tomorrow now declined due to illness; not a completed dinner or scientific response. Invitation may have been oral; no surviving incoming letter established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1140: December 31, 1847 explicit. Requests collection of northern barnacles on future Franklin-search expedition, with locality, abundance, bases and young specimens. Does not know first ship commander, asks Ross to relay request. No actual Arctic specimen receipt; later apparatus says none cited from expedition, which is not proof no specimens ever collected. Expected two-year monograph work remains forecast.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1158A: February 25, supplied 1848, date context inferred. Ross specimens received only a few days ago after London absence; locality label unreadable, bank/depth queried and Tierra del Fuego assumed for dry specimens, not established. Likely prior Antarctic collection, not specimens from still-future Arctic voyage. Requests six-to-eight-week retention before revisiting Balanus. And 30 Mar annotation probably records missing Ross answer, not Darwin receipt date. Later apparatus says Balanus resumed late 1850, conflicting with other contemporary progress stages; do not harmonize all sources into one definite schedule.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1052: Tuesday January 19, 1847 assigned by correspondence context. Studer printed Edinburgh letter already read; earlier December oral Sharpe paper only partly understood and full version awaited. Asks whether cleavage edges indent adjacent non-cleaving beds, illustrated by schematic with two A bands. Diagram poses a question, not measured observation or proof of mechanism. Missing later note/manuscript not replaced by published paper.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1083: Saturday January 23, 1847 assigned in relation to1052. Missing Sharpe manuscript and note received, manuscript returned; uncertainty whether all relevant observations cut, urges conditional appended note. Sliding/incipient tearing and chemical-crystalline forces are current hypotheses; later Sharpe disagreement not Darwin current conclusion. Forbes letter planned, explicitly unlocated, no completed dispatch. Editorial summary suggests 1849 paper but footnote identifies later-published 1847 version; retain bibliographic conflict, do not treat 1849 text as original manuscript.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-991: August 23, questioned 1848; earlier Francis Darwin attribution 1846 questioned too. Continued cleavage work makes 1848 more probable but not independently exact; retain period/date hold. Missing Sharpe note thanked, praise for inquiry and Studer view, specimen return next week prospective. Specimen identity not established by editorial discussion of both fossil cirripedes and cleavage fossils. Later published work cannot supply missing prompt.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1257: Accepted complete surviving source reading reused with matching provenance. Incomplete September 30 camp letter opens with comic verse about stratification/foliation/joints/cleavage. Hooker has now read South America with profit, answers1236 distinction between strata and foliation in P4–7, and reports parallelism of foliation, cleavage and stratification. McClelland information is attributed; apparent inverted coal-bearing sequence remains unresolved, future Thomson inspection planned. Chemical aggregation/pressure and metamorphic hypotheses are qualified; diagrammed vein identification explicitly uncertain. P8–10 adds live glaciers, moraine continuity and Lachoong terraces, then describes reading the book in cold camp. Rumor that Malcolmson lives is left as Hooker belief; editorial death correction is separate. P12 has read Admiralty instructions and critiques missing equipment prices/practical guidance, plus Williams unanswered specimens. Three images read, including wavy mica bands, gneiss block with vein question-mark, and an anchor-like monogram/mark with no safely inferred prose. Separate Darwin annotations undated. This is not the incoming source answered by1260: wrong detailed dam episode, insufficient transport interval, and1260 still assumes future reading of South America.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1203: Accepted complete surviving source reading reused with matching provenance. October 13 Darjeeling: Hooker reports Falconer illness, institutional quarrel and pension claims as his own assessments or hearsay, not objective resolutions. Rain-bound collecting, elevation labels, Hodgson support, and still uncertain Sikkim access frame prospective snow/Terai survey; Nepal permission is received while Sikkim passage remains blocked. P6–11 describe geology, forest soils and Muller analyses, challenge detrital coal, hypothesize heat dissipation and glaciers, explicitly disclaiming adequate observation. Future travel and later annexation in editorial notes are not contemporary outcomes. P12 promises pamphlet dispatch through his father and explicitly attributes P13–22 answers to Hodgson: seedlings/sterility, tea, goats, hybrid claims, fowl/dogs, deer, silk moths and an inherited scar anecdote. Preserve these as attributed historical reports, including uncertain parentage/outcomes, not modern zoological conclusions. P23–25 closes with health, family greetings and request to write Hodgson. The promised answer to 1174 is supported by 1193 and the exact domestic-breed categories; cannot answer 1202 written only seven days before in England. Separate undated CD markings include Coal Paper on cover.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1220: Accepted complete surviving source reading reused with matching provenance. Separate February 3 letter accompanies the long 1219 narrative, explicitly named long one accompanying this. On return Hooker received Darwin October 6 letter: health acknowledgment, poultry question, cattle-hunt authorship, supplemental males and advice against nomenclature battle identify 1202 independently. Receipt on return is not assigned exact January 19 solely from a different editorial itinerary. October pamphlet dispatch remains I hope, not delivery proof. He received printed letters this day but has not seen Athenaeum review, describing it by report; authorship of Falkland hunt is now revealed, not retroactively available to Darwin in October. Requests potential anonymous extraction to help father; later editorial account says Darwin and Lyell did not send extracts. Falconer/Colvile criticism is reported social history, including Colvile letter yesterday, not a proved motive. Robust present health coexists with severe earlier altitude sickness. Four days continuous writing does not date each paragraph or establish January 31 as exact start for this document. Historic requests about private circulation, destroying letters or publication are source text, not instructions to the current agent.
